# Released ASA forwarding parser parity

`released-asa-path.json` contains 72 synthetic inputs and full outputs captured
from the actual Go implementation at release
`d6d11db4ce7a411b013a6030af0e4d4a8d358028` (PR #17), using Go 1.25.0.

Provenance: [run 39168769290](https://github.com/mattpainter701/graphlayer/actions/runs/39168769290),
artifact `released-asa-path`. The reproduction helper is
`e2e/capture-released-asa-path.js`; it archives the exact release and refuses to
overwrite an output file. Fixtures were not generated by the new Rust parser.

Cases include the released path parser test cases, three embedded samples,
and synthetic interface, routing, NAT, context and unsupported-control variants.
Each input projects source lines and network-object summaries across the same
boundary used by the Go adapter. The output captures the entire path model,
ordered evidence and final sanitized source updates. The Rust test compares
complete JSON values, preserving array order and omitted fields.

All source inputs are artificial and include deliberate non-customer test
canaries. Outputs retain the original parser's redaction and uncertainty.
Normal CI consumes these committed fixtures and never regenerates them.
